div.p: Task scheduling in real-time systems is a concept by which we can schedule the tasks according to their priorities. In hard real-time systems, the task scheduling is more important due to the chance of system failure. We discuss EDF task scheduling which is an optimal technique for the uniprocessor systems. The existing result of the QPA algorithm was applied on the uniprocessor system to check the schedulability of the tasks in uniprocessor system. We have extended the QPA algorithm to check the schedulability of the task sets in multiprocessor systems. Our algorithm is based on QPA algorithm and the utilization balanced algorithm. The proposed algorithm checks the absolute deadlines much faster than the existing QPA algorithm for uniprocessor real-time systems.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Real-time systems are important parts of our life now-adays. In the last few decades, there has been an eye catching growth in the count of real-time systems, being used in domestic and industry production. A real-time system must deliver services in a timely manner. The services not only be delivered fast, but also meet some timing deadline. The application of real-time systems is in the field of defense and space systems, networked multimedia systems, embedded automative system etc. A real-time system changes its state as a function of physical time. For example, a chemical reaction continues to change its state even after its controlling computer system has stopped its functioning. Based on this a real-time system can be decomposed into a set of subsystems i.e., the controlled object, the real-time computer system and the human operator. A real-time computer system must react to stimuli from the controlled object (or the operator) within time intervals dictated by its environment. The instant before which the result should be produced is called a deadline.

In real-time scheduling theory, a real-time system comprises a set of real-time tasks. The tasks can be scheduled by a number of policies including fixed priority or dynamic priority algorithms. The success of a real-time system depends on whether all requests of the tasks can be guaranteed to complete their executions before their timing deadlines; if they can, and then we say the task set is schedulable. In our work, we have used the EDF (earliest deadline first) dynamic priority scheduling policy algorithm which was introduced by Liu and Layland [2] in 1973. It has been proven by Dertouzos [16] to be optimal among all scheduling algorithms on a uniprocessor, in the sense that if a real-time task set cannot be scheduled by EDF, then this task set cannot be scheduled by any other algorithm. Liu and Layland [2] proposed the necessary and sufficient schedulability condition for EDF scheduling algorithm under the assumption that all tasks' relative deadlines are equal to their periods. So, the scheduling condition in earliest deadline first algorithm given by Liu and Layland [2] is the total utilization of the task set is less than or equal to 1. However, in real-time systems, a task's relative deadline is not always equal to its period, so the above assumption severely restricts the usage of EDF in practice. The existing results of QPA algorithm for EDF scheduling with arbitrary relative deadlines need to calculate the processor demand of the task set at every absolute deadline to check if there is an overflow in a specified time interval. This interval is bound by a certain value which guarantees that we can find a failure point if the task set is not schedulable. In such an interval, there could be a very large number of absolute deadlines that need to be verified. In this paper, we have proposed an algorithm for EDF scheduling in multiprocessor systems with the help of utilization balanced algorithm and QPA algorithm. We have also considered task dependency in the task sets for the task scheduling. From simulation, we show the effect of task dependency on QPA algorithm which was checking the schedulability of the task set by counting the absolute deadlines. The required calculation by QPA with task dependency is stable for both uniprocessor systems and multiprocessor systems.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows: Section 2 describes the background and notations used in this paper. Section 3 describes the related work done for schedulability analysis and the existing QPA algorithm for the uniprocessor systems with EDF scheduling and arbitrary relative deadlines. Section 4 describes the proposed algorithm for schedulability analysis in multiprocessors real-time systems using QPA algorithm. In Section 5, we discuss the working of the proposed algorithm. In Section 6, the different results and comparison are shown. Conclusion and future work are given in Section 7.

div.head: II. BACKGROUND
div.p: Based on the deadline, the real-time systems are classified into three categories.

• Hard real-time system • Soft real-time system • Firm real-time system If the result of the system has utility even after the deadline has passed, the system is classified as soft, otherwise it is firm. On-line transaction systems, airline reservation systems are soft real-time systems. A real-time system is said a firm real-time system when a few missed deadlines will not to lead to total failure. For example, in video Conference, if we miss any video segment, then if it comes in future then the segment will be simply rejected. If a catastrophe could result if a deadline is missed, in the system is hard. For example, command and Control systems, Air traffic control systems are examples of hard real-time systems. In our work, we have considered hard real-time system only. There are three types of tasks involved in the realtime systems.

• Periodic task • Sporadic task • Aperiodic task Periodic Tasks are the tasks which repeat after certain fixed interval of time span. For Example, the signal from the satellite sent to the earth station at regular interval of time are periodic tasks. Sporadic Tasks are the tasks which do not occur in regular intervals of time. For Example, in a robot, a task that gets generated to handle an obstacle that suddenly appears is a sporadic task. Aperiodic Tasks are the tasks same as the sporadic tasks but two instances of the aperiodic tasks may occur simultaneously. For example, when the laptop is connected with the USB mouse and we touch the touchpad of the laptop and USB mouse at same time, we say that the tasks generated are aperiodic in nature. Here we consider the periodic tasks only.

The tasks in the real-time system are generally dependent on some other task. More general way of inter task dependency arises when a task waits for the result of another task to begin its execution. For Example, the processing of a photograph on earth station should wait for the photograph to come from the satellite. Now, we describe the notations, we have used in this paper. A hard real-time system consists of a set of n independent real-time tasks τ 1 , τ 2 , ......, τ n where each task τ i consists of an infinite or finite stream of jobs or requests which must be completed before their deadlines. Let τ i indicate any given task of the system. Each task will be periodic in nature.

The following notation is used throughout the paper. e i -execution time of task τ i . d i -deadline of the task τ i . p i -period of the task τ i . n-number of the tasks in the task set. u i -utilization of the individual tasks in the task set. U-utilization of the task set.

C. Utilization Balanced Algorithm
div.p: Utilization balanced algorithm [10] is used to assign the tasks to different processors of a multiprocessor real-time system. First this algorithm sorts the tasks in increasing order of their processor utilization. Then, the task having the lowest processor utilization is assigned to the least utilized processor. By this method, the utilizations of different processors can be balanced. Below, we present the utilization balanced algorithm in pseduocode form.

div.head: IV. PROPOSED ALGORITHM
div.p: To the best of our knowledge, there is no algorithm for schedulability analysis of multiprocessor real-time systems using QPA algorithm. In this section, we have proposed an algorithm for schedulability analysis of multiprocessor real-time system with task set having dependency in between them using the QPA algorithm, utilization balanced algorithm of multiprocessor real-time systems. We have named our proposed algorithm as MQPA (Quick convergence Processor-demand Analysis for multiprocessor real-time system) algorithm. We have already discussed the utilization balanced algorithm in pseudocode form in previous section. Here, we discuss our proposed MQPA algorithm for multiprocessor systems. First, Our MQPA algorithm checks the necessary and sufficient condition for the task to be scheduled in a multiprocessor real-time system. Second, the MQPA algorithm uses the utilization balanced algorithm to assign the tasks to the individual processors. Then, the QPA algorithm checks the schedulability of the task set in the assigned processor.

The total number of iterations taken to check the schedulability of the task set considering all the processors of the multiprocessor system is found to be less than that of the uniprocessor system. div.head: VI. EXPERIMENT AND COMPARISONS
div.p: The tasksets are the most important factors to prove that our result is better. The tasksets are created from the algorithms that we are going to discuss here.

div.head: Utilizations generation policy:
div.p: To generate the utilization of the task set and uniformly distribute the utilization into the tasks of the task set between 0 to 1, we use the UUniFast algorithm [3]. Bini and Buttazzo [3] derived the UUniFast algorithm which can efficiently generate the task utilizations with uniform distributions.

div.head: Periods generation policy:
div.p: The periods have the most significant effect on the schedulability. So, we have to generate periods of different magnitudes. We use the approach recommended by Davis and Burns [4] to generate the task periods according to an exponential distribution.

Relative deadlines generation policy: The relative deadline of each task di is generated randomly from [a,b] where a is the lower bound value of d i9 and b is the upper bound value of di. div.p: From Figures 3, 4 and 5, we can infer that the proposed algorithm is taking less iterations with variation of processor utilization of the task set having different number of tasks. Here, we have taken 1 to 4 numbers of processors and task sets with 10 tasks, 20 tasks and 40 tasks per task set. Then, the proposed algorithm is applied on the task set. In all the cases, the number of iterations to check the absolute deadline is less than the QPA Algorithm for uniprocessor systems.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: We have developed an algorithm for multiprocessor system which is a combination of utilization balanced algorithm and QPA algorithm. The proposed algorithm is named as MQPA algorithm. Utilization balanced algorithm is used to assign tasks to the processors of multiprocessor system. And the QPA algorithm is used to check the schedulability of the task sets under EDF algorithm. Our algorithm is taking taking less number of iterations than the existing QPA algorithm for uniprocessor systems.Introduction of task dependency concept into our algorithm(MQPA) can be the future work.
